rec.name: Collection Page Infinite Scroll (Toggle vs. Pagination)
rec.status: Built — launched (tested and documented; product image added to catalog)

what.text: A collection-page feature that automatically loads the next batch of products as the shopper nears the bottom of the product grid, with a loading spinner and no manual pagination. It is controlled by a checkbox in the collection section settings. When enabled, products load automatically and the pagination is hidden. When disabled, the standard pagination is shown and nothing loads automatically.

why.text: Infinite scroll removes the friction of clicking through numbered pages, so browsing feels continuous. Shoppers see more products in one session and are less likely to drop off at a page break. This can raise product views and add-to-cart rate on large collections. The toggle lets the team A/B test infinite scroll against classic pagination, since infinite scroll can hurt footer access and make it harder to return to a position in the list.

how.text: Implemented as custom code, because no existing theme had it. 1) Add a checkbox setting 'Enable Infinite Scroll' (id enable_infinite_scroll, default false) to the main-collection section schema. 2) When the setting is on, inject CSS that hides the page-pagination element (opacity 0, pointer-events none). 3) After {% endpaginate %}, render an <infinite-scroll></infinite-scroll> custom element when the setting is on. 4) In theme.js, define an InfiniteScroll custom element. It uses an IntersectionObserver (rootMargin 100px, threshold 0.1) on the pagination element. When it comes into view, it fetches the rel='next' URL and parses the HTML. It appends the new .product-item nodes into '#facet-main .product-list__inner' and refreshes the pagination markup. It stops observing when there is no next link, and shows or hides a spinner during loading. 5) In custom.css, add the spinner styles and force .product-item[reveal] to opacity 1 so the appended items are visible. The selectors are theme-specific and must be adapted to other themes.

items: Enable Infinite Scroll (checkbox in the collection section, default off)
On = automatic loading of further products, pagination hidden
Off = no automatic loading, standard pagination shown

dependencies.text: No metafield needed. Needs a theme with a main-collection section that uses {% paginate %} and a page-pagination element with a rel='next' link. Needs the theme.js custom-element base class (CustomHTMLElement) and the selectors #facet-main .product-list__inner .product-item. Needs access to edit theme.js, custom.css and the section schema, so it cannot be installed by non-developers. The theme is a Focal-style theme (inferred from CustomHTMLElement and page-pagination). The source is a Sectionfy test theme. Estimated effort was about 5 hours. The ticket calls it a 'Section', but the implementation edits the existing collection section.

items: Page load/performance (LCP, INP) with more items loaded
Conversion rate and revenue per session (A/B vs. pagination)
